groups.rationale: Second-pass lead and Astra-low review: Jagat is a uniquely corresponding named village variety under Northern Ghale (ghh), Nepal, in both registries. GRN enumerates the five distinct varieties Jagat, Khorla, Nyak, Philim and Uiya; the Glottolog-indexed Webster survey corroborates those village varieties (Korla spelling in the survey bibliography). Earlier generic-label exclusion arose from Northern in the parent name, not the leaf. Same immediate parent/kind, unique competing-name checks, no children or scalar/Scripture conflicts. Preserve all five distinct dialects while consolidating each repeated source identity.

Second-pass lead and Astra-low review: Chuksang is a uniquely corresponding village variety under Seke (skj), Nepal. GRN explicitly equates Seke with Seke (Nepal) and enumerates Chuksang, Tangbe and Tetang. Glottolog has the same direct leaves; ELA independently documents distinct village dialects including Chhusang, Tangbe and Tetang. This resolves the parent-name prefix exclusion without treating the three registry leaves as an exhaustive dialect inventory. Same immediate parent/kind, unique competing-name checks, no children or scalar/Scripture conflicts. Keep the distinct village dialects separate.
